The source gives the parent's __path__ as the path parameter and explicitly states what happens if that attribute cannot be accessed. The Python 3.13.0 import reference documents that an uncached submodule or subpackage search raises ModuleNotFoundError when the resolved parent module lacks the required __path__ attribute. The standard import machinery needs a search for the named child and an ordinary attribute lookup reports that the resolved parent module has no __path__. An absent attribute is different from an accessible empty path. A cached child or other exceptions from custom attribute access fall outside the claim. An already cached child can return during the cache lookup. A locally constructed 3.13.5 parent without __path__ prevented the child finder call, while adding __path__ reached that call.
